arguments.title: 2027 Lifecycle Systems leadership model — December 4 decision draft
arguments.hypothesis: A 2027 operating model can remove Riley from routine monthly preparation and source-closure attendance while preserving a concrete monthly hands-on audit and explicit escalation and decision rights for consequential analytical judgment.
arguments.metric_of_record: Monthly audit completion and escalation fidelity: the audit is completed against the evidence system, and every missing field, disputed semantic, cross-surface discrepancy, customer correction, incident stop, or executive-language decision is routed without silent release or authority expansion.
arguments.cohort_scope: Lifecycle Systems 2027 operating model across the existing four board-evidence lanes and governed lifecycle surfaces; no expansion of consumer scope is implied.
arguments.timeline: Draft for December 4, 2026 decision; if approved, implementation begins only on an explicitly agreed 2027 date and after transition controls are confirmed.
arguments.body:
Purpose and current-state guardrail

This is a decision draft, not an approved role change. Owen’s November 6 independent source-completeness closure and Riley’s bounded November 13 claims decision are evidence for designing a possible 2027 model, not authorization to change 2026 work. Until a decision is made and an effective date is expressly set, Riley continues attending routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews, and current authority boundaries remain unchanged.

Delegated monthly cadence

Proposed 2027 cadence, subject to December 4 approval:

1. Owen prepares the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and four-lane source-completeness packet using the established workflows, exact coverage through-dates, required fields, denominators, reporting units, exception ledger, named-owner certifications, and cross-view checks.
2. Ines performs routine lifecycle message-state governance and operator-guidance review only where governed meanings and current state are unchanged, the relevant views agree, and there is no correction, incident stop, state-changing request, ambiguity, exception-heavy case, or disputed semantics.
3. Daniela’s team retains source dependencies, transport, refresh, parsing, mappings, engineering release, and rollback controls.
4. Owen may close routine source completeness only when all required fields are present, definitions are unchanged, named owners have certified their sections, and no cross-surface discrepancy exists. The close is a source-completeness decision only.
5. Riley is removed from routine preparation and routine source-closure attendance only after the approved effective date and transition checks. Riley receives the monthly exception/escalation packet and conducts the hands-on audit described below.
6. The model remains limited to the existing four evidence lanes: Helio Start, Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge controls. No new consumer, cohort, metric, or authority is created by this draft.

Exact escalation triggers

Escalate to Riley and do not close, release, suppress, infer, or revive state when any of the following occurs:

- Any required field is missing, stale, unresolved, invalid, or conflicting, including a missing exact through-date, denominator, reporting unit, source timestamp, owner certification, or exception disposition.
- A metric, field, cohort, denominator, identity crosswalk, or governed term has disputed or changed semantics.
- Two surfaces, views, files, systems, or owner statements disagree, including a cross-surface discrepancy that could affect interpretation, eligibility, routing, suppression, hold/release state, or a claim.
- A customer correction or challenge is received or discovered.
- An incident stop, safety stop, or request to halt operation is raised.
- The proposed wording would make or imply an executive, causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, or final-claim decision.
- A request would change state meanings, add an exception path, release a field-specific hold, suppress or contact a customer, reopen a declined connection, change eligibility or routing, or expand the governed consumer scope.
- A source is late or outside freshness limits in a way that affects a governed output; alerting may identify the impact, but it does not release or override a hold.
- The evidence depends on an unsupported identity crosswalk or combines workspace, account, destination, report, exception episode, or support-labor units without a defensible common unit.
- Named-owner certification is absent, late, qualified, or inconsistent with the underlying record.

Escalation must preserve the original records, state the affected field and surface, identify the exact coverage window, record the owner and timestamp, and leave the item visibly held or incomplete until the authorized decision is recorded. A prior true value must not be reused to repair stale state, and decisions are not automatically revived.

Hands-on audit design

Riley’s monthly audit is a direct, bounded test of the evidence system rather than a return to routine line-editing. For one agreed audit slice each month, Riley will independently select or be assigned a reproducible sample spanning the active four-lane packet and, where relevant, an exception or hold episode. Riley will:

- retrieve the source records and preserve provenance, source timestamps, exact through-dates, definitions, denominators, units, and identity crosswalks;
- replay the evidence path from source fields through the reported metric, exception, hold, or operating statement;
- test at least one complete record path and one held, exception, or boundary case when available;
- compare the reported state across the relevant views and verify owner certification;
- check that stale, missing, conflicting, customer-corrected, or incident-stopped state remains held and is not silently repaired or released;
- verify that narrative language stays descriptive when the evidence is descriptive and does not overstate causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, or executive conclusions;
- record pass, finding, unresolved question, owner, timestamp, affected surface, and required disposition in a monthly audit log.

The audit should be small enough to be repeatable and large enough to exercise source completeness, governed-state handling, cross-surface consistency, and claim boundaries. The December 4 decision should set the sample rule, minimum path coverage, evidence-retention location, service-level expectation for findings, and whether an audit finding pauses the affected lane automatically or requires Riley’s explicit stop decision. Riley may expand the slice when a trigger or pattern warrants it; expansion is audit scope, not routine preparation ownership.

Decision rights

Riley retains authority over causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, executive-language, and final-claim decisions; disputed semantics; cross-surface consequences; customer corrections; incident stops; state-changing or exception authority; and final operating claims and exclusions. Nothing in delegation of preparation or source completeness narrows those rights.

Owen owns preparation, governed inventories, measurement definitions, denominators, reporting units, exception ledgers, routine evidence explanations, cross-view checks, named-owner certification tracking, and routine source-completeness closure within the exact conditions above. Owen does not own board readiness, causal claims, revenue treatment, forecast credit, executive language, or final claims.

Ines retains routine message-state governance, suppression, holds, operator guidance, and fail-closed controls within her established boundary. She does not gain eligibility, semantic-change, engineering-release, customer-correction, incident-stop, or executive-claim authority.

Daniela’s team retains transport, refresh, parsing, source dependencies, mappings, engineering release, and coordinated rollback. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership; Tomás retains the final board narrative; Priya decides organizational and resource constraints and the December 4 role-design question.

Implementation risks

- Delegation could be mistaken for transfer of claim or board authority; mitigate with a compact role reference, explicit labels on every close, and escalation examples.
- Riley’s reduced attendance could delay detection of semantic drift or cross-surface discrepancies; mitigate with the monthly hands-on audit, required exception packet, and fail-closed escalation.
- Owen could receive incomplete owner certification or exact through-dates late; mitigate with an earlier certification checkpoint and no-close rule.
- Routine work could be misclassified when a case is exception-heavy, ambiguous, customer-corrected, incident-related, or state-changing; mitigate with conservative escalation and a no-penalty escalation norm.
- The audit could become ceremonial or recreate line-by-line preparation; mitigate with reproducible sample design, direct replay, boundary cases, findings log, and a fixed review of whether findings changed controls.
- Audit findings could create unclear stop/release behavior; decide the lane-stop rule and preserve Daniela’s release/rollback and Riley’s stop authority.
- Calendar or staffing changes could take effect before approval; mitigate with an explicit effective date, transition checklist, and written confirmation that 2026 attendance continues until then.
- Metrics could be combined across incompatible units or interpreted causally; mitigate with unit/denominator fields and mandatory claim-boundary review.

December 4 decision questions

1. Approve, reject, or revise the 2027 model that removes Riley from routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance while retaining the hands-on audit?
2. If approved, what is the exact effective date, and what transition review must occur before Riley stops attending routine reviews?
3. What minimum monthly audit sample and path coverage are required, and which four-lane scope is mandatory?
4. Where is the audit log stored, who receives it, and what is the required disposition time for findings?
5. Which findings automatically hold or stop an affected lane, and which require Riley’s explicit stop decision?
6. Are the escalation triggers above complete, especially for missing fields, disputed semantics, cross-surface discrepancies, customer corrections, incident stops, and executive-language decisions?
7. How will exact through-dates, named-owner certification, unchanged definitions, denominators, reporting units, and cross-view agreement be evidenced before Owen closes routine source completeness?
8. What transition and backup coverage applies if Owen, Ines, Daniela’s team, or Riley is unavailable?
9. How will the organization verify after 30, 60, and 90 days that delegation reduced routine attendance without reducing evidence quality or silently narrowing Riley’s authority?
10. Which decision owner records the approved model, effective date, exceptions, and unchanged authority boundaries in the role reference and operating calendar?

Decision status

No role change is approved by this draft. Until the December 4 decision and an explicitly recorded effective date, Riley continues attending routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews; no 2027 cadence, audit obligation, or delegated boundary takes effect early.

arguments.title: Lifecycle Systems H2 owner-lane kickoff — July 7
arguments.body:
Purpose
Confirm the H2 work sequence and owner handoffs without changing authority, claim boundaries, or paid-test status. The sequence below was agreed at the July 7 H2 owner-lane kickoff.

Current boundaries
• The fixed 25-workspace Helio Start cohort’s final day-90 window ends August 15. No mature outcome value is being presented by this brief.
• Existing owner authorities, lifecycle controls, the source-completeness gate, and the fixed-cohort/no-new-batch boundary remain unchanged.
• Missing, stale, unresolved, invalid, or conflicting required state stays visible and held rather than inferred or repaired.

Agreed H2 sequence and ownership
1. August 15: The fixed 25-workspace Helio Start cohort’s final day-90 window ends.
2. August 16 owner certifications:
   • Customer Success certifies paid-active status and account-level support effort.
   • Owen certifies refund-adjusted collected cash.
   • Ines certifies lifecycle handling.
   • Daniela certifies paid-source attribution and source reliability.
3. By August 18: Owen independently assembles the owner-certified mature-outcome packet and may close routine source-completeness review across the four existing board-evidence lanes: Helio Start, Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge controls.
4. August 20: Riley conducts the Q3 hands-on audit, but only after four-lane closure.
5. August 23: Priya conducts the separate paid-batch decision review.

Closure gate and escalation
Owen may close routine source-completeness review by August 18 only if every required field is present, established definitions are unchanged, all named owners have certified, no cross-surface discrepancy appears, and no semantic interpretation is disputed. If any condition is not met, Owen must leave the review incomplete and escalate to Riley, identifying the missing or conflicting condition, owner, and next action. Owen independently assembles the packet but does not resolve disputed semantics or make consequential claims outside his lane.

Owen’s selected H2 goal
For the completed predeclared outcome window, Owen will independently assemble one owner-certified, review-ready mature-outcome packet. The packet will state the denominator or coverage dates and outcome window before conclusions, document exclusions and explicit measurement limits, preserve owner certifications, and remain visibly incomplete when the closure gate is not met. Retained authority
• Riley retains the independent audit, board-readiness, causal-claim, revenue-treatment, and final operating-claim decisions, as well as disputed-semantic and exception authority.
• Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership.
• Tomás Vega retains the final board narrative.
• Ines retains lifecycle governance and message-state ownership.
• Daniela retains source reliability, engineering release, and rollback control.
• Routine certification and source-completeness closure do not expand any owner’s authority.

Explicit non-decisions
This update does not declare the fixed 25-workspace cohort mature, present any mature outcome value, establish board readiness, authorize revenue or forecast treatment, set executive or board language, authorize another paid batch, reopen paid traffic, or authorize a 26th admission. Priya’s August 23 review remains a separate decision review and is not pre-authorized by this sequence.

arguments.body:
March 16, 2026 source-lock update

The four evidence lanes retain independent readiness statuses. This source-lock update supersedes any earlier interim figures for the rows below. No unsupported revenue, acquisition, pipeline, unit-economics, or forecast treatment is admitted to the board operating section.

LANE 1 — HELIO START
Readiness: not board-ready.

Evidence lane / proposed claim: Two certified mature organic cohorts satisfy the evidence conditions for reopening consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal. They permit consideration only; they do not establish paid acquisition performance, acquisition economics, paid CAC, incremental support load, scalable unit economics, pipeline, or forecast value.

Denominator and cohort evidence:
- Certified mature cohort A: 86 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows — 66 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold; $100,840 gross billed cash and $94,760 refund-adjusted collected cash; account-level support effort of 19 minutes median and 84 minutes at P90; 4/86 (4.7%) exceeded 90 support minutes; no unsupported case entered the admitted path.
- Certified mature cohort B: 91 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows — 71 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold; $108,230 gross billed cash and $102,410 refund-adjusted collected cash; account-level support effort of 18 minutes median and 79 minutes at P90; 3/91 (3.3%) exceeded 90 support minutes; no unsupported case entered the admitted path.

Cohort or coverage dates: The exact start and end dates for both sets of admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows are still missing from the certified source. This source-completeness gap is why the lane remains not board-ready.

Predeclared outcome window and completion: Day-90 status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort are complete for both certified denominators. The exact cohort-date fields needed to make the evidence board-ready are incomplete.

March 3 technical-gate decision: The two consecutive qualifying cohorts permit consideration of a capped proposal; they do not approve a proposal, paid traffic, a budget, a channel, an audience, a pipeline target, or forecast credit. Priya has not authorized proposal preparation, and separate budget approval remains required. Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026.

Measurement limits: Interpret day-90 status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and support effort together; do not reduce the gate to a single conversion or cash number. This is evidence from the bounded organic admitted path, not a paid or incremental-acquisition comparison.

Exclusions: No unsupported, manual-billing, import, migration, or agency case entered the admitted self-serve path. No paid-traffic test, paid-source attribution, or paid-channel observation is present in this lane.

Source owner: Owen, with Customer Success for account-level outcome certification.
Source or release-reliability evidence: Owen and Customer Success certified both mature packets; the locked source still omits the exact start and end dates for both cohorts. Daniela supplies source/release reliability evidence; the missing date fields remain an unresolved source-completeness limitation, not an inferred date.

Revenue and forecast treatment: Refund-adjusted collected cash is descriptive operating evidence only. No revenue attribution, paid-acquisition economics, pipeline value, forecast credit, or unit-economics claim.
Final claim owner: Riley. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership; Tomás Vega retains the final board narrative.

LANE 2 — EXPANSION ASSIST
Readiness: board-ready.

Evidence lane / proposed claim: In the narrow standing lane, Expansion Assist was observed in 18 actual exposures from December 1 through January 30: six help-or-options requests and four observed expansions. The claim is descriptive only.

Denominator: 18 actual exposures. All 18 have complete 45-day outcome windows.

Cohort or coverage dates: December 1 through January 30.

Predeclared outcome window and completion: 45 days after each exposure; complete for all 18 exposures.

Measurement limits: There was no randomized control. The evidence supports reporting observed requests and observed expansions among exposed accounts only. It does not support causal lift, attribution, conversion, revenue impact, pipeline, forecast value, or broad-rollout claims.

Exclusions: Every exposure met the standing current-state criteria. No account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure. Do not generalize beyond the stated behavior-based, state-specific lane or treat suppression criteria as evidence of commercial effect.

Source owner: Owen, for the exposure denominator, dates, and outcome-window ledger; Ines, for current-state lifecycle and suppression-state verification.
Source or release-reliability evidence: The locked exposure ledger contains 18 actual exposures with complete 45-day windows; Ines’s current-state check confirms the standing criteria at exposure; Daniela supplies the source/release mapping evidence. No randomized-control or causal-release evidence exists and none is implied.

Revenue and forecast treatment: The four observed expansions are not revenue attribution. No revenue, pipeline, forecast, conversion, or commercial-rollout credit.
Final claim owner: Riley. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership; Tomás Vega retains the final board narrative.

LANE 3 — PRICING-PAGE PATH QUALITY
Readiness: board-ready.

Evidence lane / proposed claim: Post-rollout continuity of organic pricing-page path quality from November 26 through February 28: 9,604 organic sessions; 143 of 1,981 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts (7.2%) were later routed out for an existing unsupported condition; eligible-workspace admission completion was 44.0%; account-level support time at P90 was 75 minutes.

Denominator: 9,604 organic sessions; 1,981 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts; 143 routed-out starts, or 7.2% of starts. Admission completion is reported on the eligible-workspace denominator defined by the locked path-quality source, at 44.0%; no additional count is substituted for that source-defined denominator.

Cohort or coverage dates: November 26 through February 28.

Predeclared outcome window and completion: Continuous post-rollout coverage through February 28; complete for the stated coverage period. This is not a new randomized outcome window.

Measurement limits: The control was retired November 26. Frame this as post-rollout continuity, not a treatment-versus-control result and not a new causal claim. The evidence describes routing, admission completion, and support-time behavior for organic traffic only.

Exclusions: Existing unsupported conditions are route-outs, not failures to be counted as admitted workspaces. No paid traffic, revenue lift, paid-acquisition performance, pipeline, forecast, unit-economics, or incremental claim is permitted.

Source owner: Owen, for the session, eligibility-flow, admission, and support measures.
Source or release-reliability evidence: Priya approved the path-separated organic default on November 25; Daniela moved treatment to 100% of organic traffic and retired control on November 26. Existing path-selection, eligibility, admission, and support-routing taxonomy continued unchanged. The source-lock coverage is therefore post-rollout continuity after a defined release change.

Revenue and forecast treatment: No causal, revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or unit-economics treatment. Report only the descriptive continuity measures and their denominators.
Final claim owner: Riley. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership; Tomás Vega retains the final board narrative.

LANE 4 — SYSTEM CONTROLS
Readiness: board-ready.

Evidence lane / proposed claim: System-control performance only: from January 1 through February 28, the controls covered 2,146 Customer Success auto-nudge decisions; 83 were visible field-specific holds and 2,063 proceeded or were suppressed using current state. Measurement limits: Limit the claim to system-control operation: decision handling, field-specific holds, governed-state agreement, correction/rollback observations, and source-age alert response. This is not evidence of customer outcomes, adoption, retention, causal impact, revenue, or forecast performance.

Exclusions: Do not treat proceed, suppression, or hold counts as permission to contact, customer value, commercial conversion, or revenue. Do not infer that two pre-breach alerts establish mature reliability beyond this coverage period.

Revenue and forecast treatment: No revenue, acquisition, pipeline, unit-economics, or forecast treatment. System-control performance has no board forecast credit.
Final claim owner: Riley. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership; Tomás Vega retains the final board narrative.

Helio Start remains not board-ready despite satisfying the two-cohort evidence condition, because the exact cohort start and end dates are missing and because the March 3 decision permits consideration rather than approving acquisition economics or spend.

arguments.title: November 13 final-claims review — four-lane decision brief
arguments.body:
November 13 final-claims review — four-lane decision brief

Review
November 13, 2026, 1:00–2:00 p.m. Central

Purpose
Make the final claims decisions from the first complete four-lane source packet. This brief records the certified evidence and keeps Owen’s completed source-completeness decision separate from the still-open claim decisions.

Decision status at preparation

Owen’s completed source-completeness decision

On November 6, Owen independently normalized and reconciled the engineering decision and reliability sources through October 31, 2026. He confirmed that every required field is present, established definitions are unchanged, every named owner certified their section, and no cross-surface discrepancy exists. Owen therefore closed the first complete four-lane source packet under the bounded authority Priya granted on September 24.

This closes source completeness only. It is not a causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language decision. Those decisions remain in their existing lanes.

Certified coverage and results

1. Helio Start authority-checklist evidence
Coverage: September 15–October 31, 2026.
- 148 newly admitted organic workspaces.
- 45 checklist exposures.
- 7 ordinary setup-assistance requests.
- No eligibility-route mismatch.
- No lifecycle-suppression bypass.
- No paid traffic.
- No unsupported admission.
Interpretation boundary: descriptive authority-checklist operating evidence only. It does not establish activation or support-effort improvement, change eligibility or governed-state meaning, or authorize paid acquisition.

2. Expansion Assist
Coverage: July 1–September 15, 2026, with complete 45-day windows.
- 16 actual exposures.
- 6 help-or-options requests.
- 4 observed expansions.
- No exposed account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work.
Interpretation boundary: descriptive evidence only. The exposure denominator, outcome window, and absence of active Customer Success adoption or renewal work must remain visible; this is not randomized evidence.

3. Pricing-page continuity
Coverage: July 1–October 31, 2026.
- 12,426 organic pricing-page sessions.
- 2,576 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts.
- 183 starts, or 7.1%, were later routed out for an existing unsupported condition.
- Eligible-workspace admission completion: 44.4%.
- Account-level support-time P90: 74 minutes.
Interpretation boundary: descriptive continuity evidence after the relevant control change, not a new causal test or a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast result.

4. CS auto-nudge controls
Coverage: July 1–October 31, 2026.
- 6,704 unique decisions.
- 249 visible field-specific holds.
- 6,455 decisions proceeded or were suppressed using current state.
- No governed-field disagreement.
- No customer correction.
- No rollback.
- Four source-age alerts resolved before breach.
Interpretation boundary: system-control performance only. Holds remain field-specific; the result does not establish customer or commercial outcome lift.

Final-claims decision matrix

Decision lane | Current treatment for November 13 | What is and is not decided

Causal | OPEN — no causal claim is authorized by source completeness alone. | The packet contains descriptive evidence and continuity/control evidence. No randomized causal inference is established for the four lanes; any causal language requires a separate decision in the existing authority lane.

Revenue | OPEN — do not carry revenue attribution or revenue lift from this packet. | Observed expansions and collected operating results, where present, must not be converted into revenue impact without the separately required method, attribution, and approval.

Pipeline | OPEN — no pipeline creation, contribution, or target treatment. | The packet does not authorize pipeline credit or a pipeline statement. Expansion Assist exposures and observed expansions remain bounded evidence, not a pipeline measure.

Forecast | OPEN — no forecast credit or forecast change. | Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership. No lane result changes the forecast unless separately reviewed and approved there.

Board-readiness | OPEN — source completeness is not board readiness. | Owen’s closure confirms that the evidence packet is complete under the source-closure rules; it does not decide which lane is board-ready or permit a board claim. Riley retains the board-readiness and final operating-claims decision.

Executive-language | OPEN — no executive or board wording is approved by this brief. | Tomás owns the final board narrative; Riley retains executive-language judgment for operating claims, limits, disputed semantics, and exclusions. Any language must preserve denominators, coverage dates, outcome windows, evidence limits, and the no-overclaim boundaries above.

Required discussion at the review

- Confirm that Owen’s source-completeness closure is accepted as complete and is not treated as approval of any claim.
- Decide each of the six claim lanes independently: causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language.
- Preserve exact coverage dates, denominators, outcome windows, and lane-specific limits in any approved language.
- Keep descriptive operating evidence separate from causal inference, commercial attribution, forecast treatment, board readiness, and narrative approval.
- Record any exclusions, unresolved decisions, owner, and next review date rather than carrying an implicit claim.

Owner boundaries

- Owen: completed bounded source-completeness decision and closure-and-exception summary; no authority over causal claims, revenue treatment, forecast credit, board readiness, or executive language.
- Riley: final operating claims, causal and revenue judgment, board-readiness, executive language, disputed semantics, and exclusions.
- Marcus Vail: forecast ownership.
- Tomás: final board narrative.
- Ines and Daniela: their existing lifecycle-governance, source-reliability, engineering-release, and rollback lanes remain unchanged.

Bottom line

The first complete four-lane source packet is closed for completeness through October 31, 2026. No final claim has been approved by that closure. The November 13 review must make six explicit, separate decisions and must not let a complete source packet silently become a causal, commercial, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language approval.

arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2026 year-end self-review working draft

First complete draft — October 9, 2026

Evidence-grounded contributions

I strengthened the quality and usefulness of Lifecycle Systems evidence by keeping each claim inside its approved Q1 and Q2 boundary. I treated Expansion Assist as descriptive December 1–January 30 evidence (18 exposures, six help/options requests, and four observed expansions), not as randomized, causal, revenue, pipeline, or forecast evidence. I treated pricing-page path quality as continuity evidence rather than a new causal claim, and I kept system controls within the January 1–February 28 window: 2,146 auto-nudge decisions, 83 visible holds, no governed-field disagreement, customer correction, or rollback, and two source-age alerts before breach. I also made the four-consumer shared-state scope, field-specific holds, source ownership, denominators, and decision boundaries explicit so that incomplete evidence could not silently become executive language.

For Helio Start, I helped close the fixed 50-workspace paid cohort with reconciled attribution and certified day-90 outcomes: 37 paid-active, six canceled, four past due, and three on billing hold; $56,230 refund-adjusted collected cash; 104-minute P90 account-level support effort; and seven workspaces above 90 support minutes. I retained first integration as a leading indicator and described the result as paid-source evidence, not causal proof, because there was no randomized control. The work produced a clear decision rather than an inflated success narrative.

Leadership through delegation

I created more operating leverage by separating delegated preparation and routine source review from consequential judgment. Owen’s transition now covers monthly preparation, governed inventories, evidence assembly, cross-view checks, and bounded routine source-completeness closure. He can check packets against required denominators or coverage dates, outcome windows, exclusions, source owners, reliability evidence, reconciliation, and named-owner certification. However, missing fields, disputed semantics, source gaps, absent certifications, material corrections, cross-surface discrepancies, and proposed causal, revenue, or forecast language remain incomplete and escalate.

This is a bounded transition, not an exit from the work. I continue to participate in routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews, and I retain authority over consequential analytical judgment, claim approval, disputed semantics, cross-surface conflicts, board readiness, forecast and revenue treatment, material exceptions, executive language, and stop decisions. Delegating assembly or routine checking does not delegate those decisions.

I also supported the organic authority-checklist release as a narrow setup intervention. The checklist appears only for admitted workspaces when external-system authority is current and verified yes and the selected connector requires an owner-level permission or network-allowlist action. It changes setup guidance only. Eligibility, admission, assisted routing, fail-closed handling, and the meanings of governed states remain unchanged: missing, stale, conflicting, pending, no, and not-sure states continue through their existing treatment. The checklist does not establish contact permission, release a hold, or authorize a customer action.

Boundary defended under pressure

The clearest boundary decision was declining a second Helio Start paid batch and any Q4 pipeline or forecast credit. At the August 21 review, the 37 paid-active workspaces and $56,230 collected cash could have been presented as justification to scale. I instead weighed the support tail—104-minute P90 and seven high-support workspaces—against the absence of control evidence and mature scalable-economics evidence. Priya accepted the recommendation: the cohort remains closed, paid traffic remains off, and no second batch or forecast treatment is authorized. I also preserved the existing admission rules rather than weakening them to improve apparent conversion.

The subsequent seven-case review reinforced the same boundary. Five cases required a supported owner-level permission or network-allowlist action after admission, and two were ordinary integration troubleshooting; none showed defective authority definitions, stale state, conflicting state, billing problems, or unsupported admission. The resulting checklist addresses demonstrated post-admission setup friction without changing what external-system authority means or turning a preparation aid into a new eligibility decision.

Development priorities

First, I will make delegation measurable without abandoning the operating work. I will complete Owen’s three-to-five-packet observation period while continuing my own monthly preparation and source-closure reviews. For each comparable packet, I will record denominator and coverage completeness, certification status, cross-surface reconciliation, correction rate, and the issues that required escalation. If the evidence supports a narrower handoff, I will document exactly which routine checks can move and which claims and exceptions remain with me; if not, I will keep the current bounded model.

Second, I will turn the authority-checklist learning into a disciplined improvement loop. I will complete the seven-case workback, review checklist outcomes with Ines, Daniela, Owen, and Customer Success, and separate setup-sequence observations from any claim about eligibility, authority meaning, causality, or commercial impact. I will use the October review to identify a small number of measurable checks—such as checklist display accuracy, completion, routing outcome, and remaining support effort—while preserving the current verified-yes trigger and all existing fail-closed boundaries.

Across both priorities, my goal is greater leverage with explicit ownership and evidence, not a premature claim that routine preparation or source-closure responsibility has moved away from me.

Owen and Customer Success supplied a clean descriptive four-week operating read: 92 admitted organic workspaces, 28 checklist exposures, and five ordinary setup-assistance requests. The read found no eligibility mismatch, route mismatch, lifecycle-suppression issue, paid-source traffic, or unsupported admission. It was descriptive only; there was no randomized control, and the counts do not establish an activation improvement or a support-effort improvement.

I kept the checklist as a standard part of organic onboarding rather than turning the counts into an activation or support-effort claim. The checklist remains limited to admitted workspaces when external-system authority is current and verified yes and the selected connector requires an owner-level permission or network-allowlist action. It changes setup guidance only. Eligibility, admission, assisted routing, fail-closed handling, and the meanings of governed states remain unchanged. Missing, stale, conflicting, pending, no, and not-sure states continue through their existing treatment.

I also made the maintenance split explicit. Ines may revise connector-specific instructional wording only; the required owner action, trigger conditions, and governed state meanings remain unchanged. Daniela owns connector-detection logic and must approve any connector-detection or release-behavior change, with engineering release and rollback controls retained. I retain eligibility decisions, state meanings, evidence interpretation, claim boundaries, and any proposed change to those semantics. The checklist does not establish contact permission, release a hold, or authorize a customer action.

This is a bounded transition, not an exit from the work. I continue to participate in routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews, and I retain authority over consequential analytical judgment, claim approval, disputed semantics, cross-surface conflicts, board readiness, forecast and revenue treatment, material exceptions, executive language, and stop decisions. Delegating assembly, maintenance tasks, or routine checking does not delegate those decisions.

Boundary defended under pressure

The clearest boundary decision was declining a second Helio Start paid batch and any Q4 pipeline or forecast credit. At the August 21 review, the 37 paid-active workspaces and $56,230 collected cash could have been presented as justification to scale. I instead weighed the support tail—104-minute P90 and seven high-support workspaces—against the absence of control evidence and mature scalable-economics evidence. Priya accepted the recommendation: the cohort remains closed, paid traffic remains off, and no second batch or forecast treatment is authorized. I also preserved the existing admission rules rather than weakening them to improve apparent conversion.

The subsequent seven-case review reinforced the same boundary. Five cases required a supported owner-level permission or network-allowlist action after admission, and two were ordinary integration troubleshooting; none showed defective authority definitions, stale state, conflicting state, billing problems, or unsupported admission. The resulting checklist addresses demonstrated post-admission setup friction without changing what external-system authority means or turning a preparation aid into a new eligibility decision.

Development priorities

First, I will make delegation measurable without abandoning the operating work. I will complete Owen’s three-to-five-packet observation period while continuing my own monthly preparation and source-closure reviews. For each comparable packet, I will record denominator and coverage completeness, certification status, cross-surface reconciliation, correction rate, and the issues that required escalation. If the evidence supports a narrower handoff, I will document exactly which routine checks can move and which claims and exceptions remain with me; if not, I will keep the current bounded model.

Second, I will turn the authority-checklist learning into a disciplined improvement loop. I will review the October four-week read with Ines, Daniela, Owen, and Customer Success, and separate setup-sequence observations from any claim about eligibility, authority meaning, causality, activation, support effort, or commercial impact. I will use the descriptive operating read to identify a small number of measurable checks—such as checklist display accuracy, completion, routing outcome, and remaining support effort—while preserving the current verified-yes trigger and all existing fail-closed boundaries.

Across both priorities, my goal is greater leverage with explicit ownership and evidence, not a premature claim that routine preparation or source-closure responsibility has moved away from me.

arguments.body:
Helio Start capped paid-acquisition proposal — Q2 2026 working draft

Status and purpose

Working draft prepared after Priya authorized preparation of a capped Q2 paid-acquisition proposal. This document is a proposal for review, not an approval, launch authorization, budget approval, or authorization to purchase traffic. No paid campaign, audience, spend, experiment, or launch is authorized by this document.

Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. Any Q2 paid-acquisition motion would require subsequent explicit approval, including separate budget approval, before implementation. No pipeline target, pipeline credit, forecast credit, or forecastable revenue attribution is included or proposed here.

Evidence basis: two qualifying mature cohorts

The evidence gate for reopening consideration is satisfied: two consecutive mature cohorts each had fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 minutes of account-level support effort, and no unsupported case entered the admitted path. Satisfying this evidence condition permits preparation and review of a proposal; it does not approve the proposal, paid traffic, a budget, a launch, or any commercial claim.

1. January 27, 2026 mature cohort

- 86 admitted workspaces.
- $94,760 refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Account-level support effort: 19-minute median and 84-minute P90.
- 4 of 86 accounts exceeded 90 support minutes (4.7%), below the 5% evidence threshold.
- No unsupported case entered the admitted path.

2. February 24, 2026 mature cohort

- 91 admitted workspaces.
- Day-90 status: 71 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold.
- $108,230 gross billed cash and $102,410 refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Account-level support effort: 18-minute median and 79-minute P90.
- 3 of 91 accounts exceeded 90 support minutes (3.3%), below the 5% evidence threshold.
- No unsupported case entered the admitted path.

Interpretation and limits

Taken together, the cohorts provide the evidence required to reopen consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal. They do not establish paid CAC, incremental support load from paid traffic, scalable paid-channel unit economics, paid-channel performance, pipeline value, forecast value, or revenue attribution. Day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort must remain visible together; they must not be reduced to one conversion number. Cohort dates, denominators, outcome windows, units, and exclusions must remain explicit in any subsequent review. The cohort-date limitation remains unresolved, and the proposal remains not board-ready.

Operating boundaries that remain unchanged

The proposal preserves the existing Helio Start operating contract:

- Eligibility remains a prerequisite to admission. The proposal does not broaden eligibility or create an additive exception score.
- Refusal boundaries remain in force. Unsupported conditions are refused or routed out rather than admitted by paid-acquisition intent.
- Connector access is not equivalent to owner-level external-system authority, and neither is equivalent to permission for automated contact.
- External-system authority must be documented in the authoritative source with source, timestamp, and relevant permission or allowlist evidence before eligibility and messaging checks are rerun. Authentication, connector access, entitlement, administrator proof, or historical values alone do not establish owner-level authority.
- The five separately governed fields remain separate: external-system authority, connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin status, and active Customer Success adoption or renewal work. Missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting state creates a visible field-specific hold; prior true values are not reused to repair stale state.
- Lifecycle rules, suppression rules, and active Customer Success adoption or renewal-work suppressions remain unchanged. A proceed result is not blanket permission to contact.
- Instrumentation and existing event taxonomy remain unchanged unless separately reviewed and approved. Admission, path-selection, eligibility, support-routing, lifecycle, and outcome events must retain their current meanings and identity crosswalks.
- Support routing remains fail-closed and unchanged. Unsupported, ambiguous, exception-heavy, disputed-semantics, customer-correction, incident-stop, or state-changing conditions do not become routine paid-acquisition traffic.
- Daniela retains engineering release and rollback authority. Ines’s routine messaging-state authority does not extend across Helio Start paid acquisition or engineering controls. Riley retains high-risk judgment, customer-correction and incident-stop authority, cross-surface consequences, and executive claims. Owen retains denominators, measurement definitions, governed inventories, exception ledgers, and routine evidence explanations.

Open decisions — no placeholder choice is settled

The sections below identify decisions required for any later approval. The listed alternatives, if any, are prompts for decision-making only and are not selected values.

Traffic cap

Decision required: define the maximum paid traffic exposure for the proposal, including the unit, time window, audience denominator, pacing rule, and whether the cap applies to impressions, clicks, sessions, eligibility-flow starts, or admitted workspaces.

Open questions:
- What exact cap and unit should apply?
- What is the maximum concurrent exposure and the maximum cumulative exposure?
- Who may pause or reduce traffic when a guardrail is approached?
- What evidence is required before increasing any cap?

Status: unresolved. No traffic cap has been approved or selected.

Budget request

Decision required: define a separate budget request, including total ceiling, period, spend pacing, instrument of record, and whether unused funds expire or can be reallocated.

Open questions:
- What amount, if any, should be requested?
- Which approver owns the budget decision, and what Finance review is required?
- What conditions must be met before any funds are released?

Status: unresolved. No budget is approved, allocated, or implied by this draft.

Audience and channel

Decision required: specify the eligible audience, exclusions, geography or account constraints, channel(s), creative or landing-surface scope, and whether any audience may enter the existing admitted path.

Open questions:
- Which audience and channel, if any, should be evaluated?
- What exclusion logic and suppression refresh requirements apply before exposure?
- How will paid traffic be distinguished from organic traffic without changing existing lifecycle, eligibility, refusal, connector-access, authority, or support-routing semantics?

Status: unresolved. No audience, channel, creative, or landing-surface choice is settled.

Success measure

Decision required: predeclare the primary and supporting measures, denominators, paid-source attribution span, attribution window, maturity window, and analysis method before any exposure.

Paid-source attribution must remain visible and attributable from the start of the eligibility flow through admission. The source value and identity crosswalk must not be dropped, overwritten, or collapsed into an aggregate before admission, and paid-source attribution must not be used to bypass any existing eligibility, refusal, lifecycle, suppression, or support-routing rule.

The measure set must keep separate, at minimum:
- paid exposure and eligible/admitted denominators, with paid-source attribution visible from eligibility-flow start through admission;
- day-7 first integration, which may be used as a leading operating indicator only and is not a mature outcome claim;
- complete-window mature day-90 status, including paid-active status;
- refund-adjusted collected cash, with gross billed cash shown separately, only after the applicable complete outcome window;
- account-level support effort, including support minutes from the first contact, median, P90, and the count and percentage exceeding 90 minutes, only after the applicable complete outcome window;
- unsupported admissions, with an explicit zero-tolerance guardrail;
- assisted-route reasons, captured at the first assisted contact and retained at the account level.

Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort require complete outcome windows before they support a mature claim. Day-7 first integration may inform operating monitoring while those windows are incomplete, but it must be labeled as leading and must not be substituted for the mature measures.

Open questions:
- Which measure is primary for the decision, and which are guardrails or descriptive outcomes?
- What complete outcome window and attribution rules are required?
- What minimum evidence would justify continuation, pause, or closure?

Status: unresolved. No conversion, CAC, revenue, pipeline, or forecast measure has been selected or authorized.

Support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails

Decision required: confirm the operating thresholds, measurement window, escalation path, and action for any breach.

Evidence-based constraints carried into this draft:
- The reopening condition was fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes in each of two consecutive mature cohorts; this condition allowed proposal preparation but does not by itself define a paid-test continuation rule.
- Unsupported cases must not enter the admitted path. Any unsupported case entering the admitted path is an immediate stop condition requiring traffic hold and review; this draft does not create an exception.
- Customer Success must capture the reason for every assisted route and account-level support minutes from the first contact. Missing first-contact assisted-route reason or support-minute capture is an instrumentation and operating breach requiring a hold and review; it does not permit imputation or a relaxed denominator.
- Support effort must be measured at account level with stated denominators and complete windows. Median alone is insufficient; P90 and the >90-minute tail must remain visible.

Open questions:
- Should the same <5% tail threshold apply to any paid cohort, and what minimum denominator is required?
- What additional support-load signal or escalation threshold is needed?
- Which team owns first response, evidence certification, and the decision to hold traffic?

Status: unresolved. No paid-test thresholds or breach policy beyond the preserved admission/refusal boundary are settled; the immediate unsupported-admission stop condition is not open.

Monitoring and stop rules

Decision required: define the monitoring cadence, dashboard or source of record, alert recipients, review quorum, and any additional automatic or manual stop conditions.

Monitoring must cover, at minimum:
- paid-source attribution continuity from eligibility-flow start through admission, including the source field, timestamps, and identity crosswalk;
- eligibility, refusal, and unsupported-condition counts;
- connector authentication, connector access, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, and external-authority state;
- active Customer Success adoption or renewal-work suppression and current-state suppression behavior;
- existing lifecycle branches, path-selection, admission, and support-routing outcomes; paid source must use these existing branches and suppression behavior rather than a paid-source bypass;
- assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes captured from the first Customer Success contact;
- instrumentation completeness and identity crosswalk integrity;
- day-7 first integration as a leading operating indicator, clearly separated from complete-window mature outcomes;
- spend, exposure, paid/organic separation, and cohort maturity;
- paid-active status, refund-adjusted cash, and gross billed cash only with complete outcome windows for mature claims;
- account-level support median, P90, and >90-minute tail only with complete outcome windows for mature claims.

Immediate stop conditions:
- any unsupported case enters the admitted path;
- any paid-source attribution is missing, overwritten, or no longer traceable between eligibility-flow start and admission;
- any paid-source path bypasses an existing eligibility, refusal, lifecycle branch, current-state suppression, connector-access, external-authority, entitlement, or support-routing control;
- any field-specific hold, customer correction, incident stop, or governed-state conflict is bypassed or treated as permission to proceed.

These conditions require an immediate traffic hold and review. Other potential stop triggers requiring an explicit proposal decision include instrumentation failure, broken paid/organic separation, support-load breach, or any unapproved spend or audience expansion. No monitoring schedule, alert threshold, or additional automatic stop rule is approved by this draft.

Status: unresolved, except that the immediate stop conditions above are required operating boundaries and are not optional implementation choices.

Refund-adjusted cash treatment

Decision required: establish the cash definition, refund and credit treatment, timing, source of record, and reporting cadence.

This draft preserves the existing treatment: gross billed cash and refund-adjusted collected cash are reported separately. Refund-adjusted collected cash is the relevant collected-cash measure for evidence review; it must not be presented as paid-channel incrementality or converted into pipeline or forecast credit. Cohort maturity and refund timing must be stated, and any later paid analysis must preserve the same definitions rather than switching metrics after exposure.

Open questions:
- Which refunds, credits, reversals, and timing adjustments are included?
- What source and reconciliation owner certify the figure?
- How will paid-channel cash be reported without implying causal or incremental revenue attribution?

Status: definition boundary is preserved; detailed proposal-specific reporting decisions remain unresolved.

Decision owners and approvals required

- Riley: proposal preparation, evidence interpretation, high-risk analytical judgment, claims and exclusions, and recommendation language. Riley is not authorizing launch or spend through this draft.
- Priya: organizational/resource constraints and decision on whether the proposal may advance. Her authorization to prepare this working draft is not launch or budget approval.
- Separate budget approver / Finance owner: to be identified and to approve or reject any budget request. No budget approval is implied here.
- Owen: denominators, cohort certification, measurement definitions, complete outcome windows, governed inventories, exception ledger, and routine evidence explanations.
- Ines: lifecycle messaging-state review, suppression, holds, and operator guidance within her existing lane. Her authority does not expand to paid-acquisition launch, engineering release, or cross-surface approval.
- Daniela: transport, refresh, parsing, source dependencies, mappings, engineering release, and rollback. No release or rollback change is authorized by this draft.
- Customer Success/support owner: to be identified for support-load operations, routing, and first-response escalation; this draft does not assign a new authority.
- Marcus Vail: forecast ownership remains separate; no forecast credit is proposed.
- Tomás: final board narrative remains separate from this working draft; no board claim or forecastable growth claim is authorized here.

Required decision sequence before any launch consideration

1. Validate the two mature cohorts and all denominators, dates, complete outcome windows, refund-adjusted cash treatment, and support measures.
2. Resolve the open traffic-cap, budget, audience/channel, success-measure, guardrail, monitoring, stop-rule, and owner decisions.
3. Complete any required Finance, resource, lifecycle, instrumentation, support-routing, privacy, and engineering reviews.
4. Obtain explicit approval for the proposal and separate budget approval.
5. Obtain an explicit launch authorization that names the approved audience, channel, cap, budget, measurement plan, stop rules, and release owner.
6. Only after those approvals, run a final fail-closed preflight; a proceed result remains limited and is not blanket permission to contact.

Not approved or authorized by this draft

- No paid traffic or campaign launch.
- No budget allocation or spend.
- No audience, channel, creative, landing-surface, cap, or pacing selection.
- No change to eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, lifecycle, suppression, instrumentation, or support-routing rules.
- No exception for unsupported cases or stale, missing, unresolved, or conflicting governed state.
- No pipeline target, pipeline credit, forecast credit, paid CAC claim, incremental revenue claim, scalable unit-economics claim, or paid-performance claim.
- No general availability, broad rollout, or automatic expansion of any existing authority.

Current status

Prepared working draft only. Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. The two-of-two evidence condition supports reopening consideration and preparation of this proposal; it does not settle the open decisions or authorize approval, budget, traffic, or launch. The missing cohort dates remain unresolved, and the proposal remains not board-ready.

- assisted-route reasons, captured at the first assisted contact and retained at the account level.

Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort require complete outcome windows before they support a mature claim. Day-7 first integration may inform operating monitoring while those windows are incomplete, but it must be labeled as leading and must not be substituted for the mature measures. No conversion, CAC, revenue, pipeline, or forecast measure is selected or authorized by this draft.

Monitoring and stop rules

Monitoring for either option must cover, at minimum:

- paid-source attribution continuity from eligibility-flow start through admission, including source field, timestamps, and identity crosswalk;
- eligibility, refusal, and unsupported-condition counts;
- connector authentication, connector access, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, and external-authority state;
- active Customer Success adoption or renewal-work suppression and current-state suppression behavior;
- existing lifecycle branches, path-selection, admission, and support-routing outcomes; paid source must use these existing branches and suppression behavior rather than a paid-source bypass;
- assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes captured from the first Customer Success contact;
- instrumentation completeness and identity crosswalk integrity;
- day-7 first integration as a leading operating indicator, clearly separated from complete-window mature outcomes;
- spend, exposure, paid/organic separation, caps, and cohort maturity;
- paid-active status, refund-adjusted cash, and gross billed cash only with complete outcome windows for mature claims;
- account-level support median, P90, and >90-minute tail only with complete outcome windows for mature claims.

Immediate stop conditions for either option:

- any unsupported applicant enters the admitted path;
- any paid-source path bypasses an existing eligibility, refusal, lifecycle branch, current-state suppression, connector-access, external-authority, entitlement, or support-routing control;
- any field-specific hold, customer correction, incident stop, or governed-state conflict is bypassed or treated as permission to proceed;
- any unapproved spend, audience expansion, or cap expansion occurs.

Pause conditions for either option:

- a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source reconciliation from eligibility-flow start through admission;
- after at least 20 admissions, more than 10% of admitted accounts exceed 90 support minutes.

A pause or stop requires traffic hold and review. No result may be inferred while paid-source reconciliation is unavailable, and no mature commercial or scale decision may be made before the complete outcome windows close.

Refund-adjusted cash treatment

Gross billed cash and refund-adjusted collected cash are reported separately. Refund-adjusted collected cash is the relevant collected-cash measure for evidence review; it must not be presented as paid-channel incrementality or converted into pipeline or forecast credit. Cohort maturity and refund timing must be stated, and any later paid analysis must preserve the same definitions rather than switching metrics after exposure. The complete-window requirement remains in force for either option.

Approvals, decision owners, and required sequence

Both options remain unapproved. Separate budget approval remains required. Priya’s authorization to prepare this working draft is not launch or budget approval.

- Riley: proposal preparation, evidence interpretation, high-risk analytical judgment, claims and exclusions, and recommendation language. Riley is not authorizing launch or spend through this draft.
- Priya: organizational/resource constraints and decision on whether the proposal may advance.
- Separate budget approver / Finance owner: to be identified and to approve or reject any budget request. No budget approval is implied here.
- Owen: denominators, cohort certification, measurement definitions, complete outcome windows, governed inventories, exception ledger, and routine evidence explanations.
- Ines: lifecycle messaging-state review, suppression, holds, and operator guidance within her existing lane. Her authority does not expand to paid-acquisition launch, engineering release, or cross-surface approval.
- Daniela: transport, refresh, parsing, source dependencies, mappings, engineering release, and rollback. No release or rollback change is authorized by this draft.
- Customer Success/support owner: support-load operations, routing, and first-response escalation; this draft does not assign a new authority.
- Marcus Vail: forecast ownership remains separate; no forecast credit is proposed.
- Tomás: final board narrative remains separate from this working draft; no board claim or forecastable growth claim is authorized here.

Required sequence before any launch consideration:

1. Validate the two mature cohorts and all denominators, dates, complete outcome windows, refund-adjusted cash treatment, and support measures.
2. Confirm the recommended six-week high-intent paid-search shape or, if necessary, the smaller fallback; no third equal-weight scenario is proposed here.
3. Complete required Finance, resource, lifecycle, instrumentation, support-routing, privacy, and engineering reviews.
4. Obtain explicit approval for the proposal and separate budget approval.
5. Obtain explicit launch authorization naming the approved option, audience, channel, cap, budget, measurement plan, stop rules, and release owner.
6. Only after those approvals, run a final fail-closed preflight; a proceed result remains limited and is not blanket permission to contact.

Not approved or authorized by this draft

- No paid traffic before April 1, 2026.
- No paid traffic, campaign launch, budget allocation, or spend without explicit approval and separate budget approval.
- No change to eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, lifecycle, suppression, instrumentation, or support-routing rules.
- No exception for unsupported cases or stale, missing, unresolved, or conflicting governed state.
- No pipeline target, pipeline credit, forecast credit, paid CAC claim, incremental revenue claim, scalable unit-economics claim, or paid-performance claim.
- No general availability, broad rollout, or automatic expansion of any existing authority.

Current status

Prepared working draft only. The recommended six-week high-intent paid-search proposal and smaller fallback are both unapproved and remain subject to separate budget approval. Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026, with no paid traffic before April 1. The two-of-two evidence condition supports reopening consideration and preparation of this proposal; it does not authorize approval, budget, traffic, or launch. The missing cohort dates remain unresolved, and the proposal remains not board-ready.

arguments.body:
Helio Start capped paid-acquisition proposal — Q2 2026 working draft

PURPOSE AND STATUS

This document records the bounded Helio Start paid-acquisition proposal, subsequent pilot decisions, operating evidence, and final second-batch decision. It is not a standing authorization to change admission, lifecycle, suppression, support-routing, instrumentation, authority, or forecast rules.

The two consecutive mature organic cohorts satisfied the evidence condition for reopening consideration only:
- 86 workspaces admitted October 1–28, 2025; 4 of 86 (4.7%) exceeded 90 support minutes; no unsupported case entered the admitted path.
- 91 workspaces admitted October 29–November 25, 2025; 3 of 91 (3.3%) exceeded 90 support minutes; no unsupported case entered the admitted path.

Those cohorts supported preparation and review of a capped proposal, not launch authorization, paid CAC, scalable unit economics, causal acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast claims. Day-90 status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort remain paired rather than reduced to one conversion number.

OPERATING BOUNDARIES

Eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, lifecycle, current-state suppression, instrumentation, identity-crosswalk, and support-routing rules remain unchanged. Unsupported, stale, missing, unresolved, conflicting, disputed, or exception-heavy states remain fail-closed. Connector access, authentication, entitlement, administrator proof, or historical values do not establish owner-level external-system authority. Paid source does not bypass any existing path or suppression rule.

Paid-source attribution must remain visible from eligibility-flow start through every final route and admission. Customer Success must record assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes from first contact. An unsupported admission is an immediate stop. Attribution reconciled for all 50, no unsupported applicant entered the admitted path, no routing or instrumentation failure required a pause, and four of 50 exceeded 90 support minutes (8%), below the then-applicable pause threshold.

On May 25, all 50 admissions had complete day-7 windows; 39 of 50 reached first integration. This remains leading operating evidence only, not mature acquisition, commercial, scale, pipeline, or forecast evidence.

AUGUST 7, 2026 — PRE-CERTIFICATION DECISION GATE

The pilot remained closed at the fixed 50-workspace cohort with paid traffic off. The day-90 source-certification review was distinct from any later decision. Owen and Customer Success were required to certify mutually exclusive day-90 statuses, gross billed cash, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort, paid-source reconciliation, and unsupported-admission status. Source completeness did not itself authorize another batch, traffic, spend, audience expansion, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or causal or predictive claims.

AUGUST 17, 2026 — CERTIFIED MATURE-OUTCOME PACKET

Owen and Customer Success certified complete outcomes for all 50 workspaces in the closed high-intent paid-search cohort:

The Helio Start second-batch decision review concluded that the fixed 50-workspace cohort does not justify a second paid batch or Q4 forecast treatment. The 37 paid-active workspaces and $56,230 in refund-adjusted collected cash are descriptive cohort outcomes only. The absence of a randomized control, the 104-minute support-effort P90, and seven of 50 workspaces exceeding 90 support minutes do not support reopening paid acquisition.

Riley recommended neither a second paid batch nor Q4 forecast treatment, and Priya accepted that recommendation. Paid traffic remains off. No second Helio Start paid batch will open in Q3. The cohort receives no pipeline or forecast credit. The pilot remains closed, and all existing admission, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, suppression, and support-routing rules remain in force.

Riley owns the final claim and exclusion language. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership; Tomás retains the final board narrative.
Revenue/forecast treatment: Descriptive only; no revenue or forecast credit.

Claim: Post-rollout continuity evidence shows the operating behavior of the pricing-page path after control retirement; it is not a second causal test or a revenue result.
Denominator and window: November 26, 2025 through February 28, 2026, covering 9,604 organic sessions; 143 of 1,981 route-outs (7.2%), 44.0% admission completion, and 75-minute support-time P90.

Historical comparison note — Helio Start exclusions from Q1 and Q2 2026 board evidence

Purpose

For new board-operations reviewers: Helio Start was excluded from both approved quarterly operating-evidence sections, but for different quarter-specific reasons. Do not summarize either exclusion as generic “immaturity.”

Q1 2026 package — evidence gate and forecast treatment

Helio Start’s two qualifying mature organic cohorts satisfied the operating condition for reopening consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal: each cohort had fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 minutes of account-level support effort, and no unsupported case entered the admitted path. That evidence supported proposal consideration only. It did not create Q2 forecast credit, establish a commercial result, authorize paid traffic or an approved budget, provide acquisition evidence, or support pipeline treatment.

The lane remained not board-ready and was excluded because the row still lacked the exact start and end dates for both cohorts required by the January 6 readiness gate. The gate was preserved rather than weakened. Helio Start therefore did not appear in the approved Q1 board operating-evidence section.

The other three approved Q1 lanes remained bounded as follows:

- Expansion Assist: descriptive operating evidence for the narrow behavior-based, state-specific lane; no randomized control and no causal, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claim.
- Pricing-page path quality: post-rollout continuity evidence after control retirement; not a second causal test or a revenue result, and no pipeline or forecast credit.
- CS auto-nudge system controls: system-control operation and bounded fail-closed hold behavior during continuous coverage; not customer or commercial impact, and no causal, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claim.

Q2 2026 package — day-7 lead versus mature outcome evidence

The approved Q2 section excluded Helio Start for a different reason: the fixed 50-workspace paid pilot had a complete day-7 read but not yet complete mature outcome windows. Owen certified that 39 of 50 reached first integration by day 7. This established a leading operating indicator for the paid-source cohort and supported monitoring of the predeclared operating measure.

It did not establish acquisition success, growth, scale, paid-channel performance, revenue, pipeline value, forecast value, or a basis for a second paid batch. Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort still required complete day-90 windows before mature claims or a separate commercial decision. No acquisition or forecast claim was added.

The other three approved Q2 lanes retained their approved interpretations:

- Expansion Assist: descriptive only, with no causal, revenue, pipeline, or forecast treatment.
- Pricing-page path quality: post-rollout continuity evidence rather than a new causal result; no revenue, pipeline, or forecast treatment.
- CS auto-nudge: evidence limited to system-control performance, not customer or commercial impact.

Reviewer takeaway

Q1 excluded Helio Start because the board-readiness/source gate was incomplete: the exact cohort dates were missing, even though the operating evidence permitted consideration of a capped proposal. Q2 excluded it because the paid pilot’s day-7 result was only a leading operating read; the complete mature outcome windows needed for commercial, acquisition, or forecast interpretation had not closed. The approved three-lane interpretations in both packages remained bounded and unchanged.

input.body:
ROASTED-CHICKEN THREE-RUN DECISION-EVIDENCE SHEET
Archive date: January 1, 2028
Runs: June 28, July 26, and August 16, 2024

Scope
Compact archive of controlled sale-run evidence only. It records production performance, customer sell-through, disposition, and run economics. It does not make or reopen a menu decision.

Fixed controls
- Same 30-pound raw case and tested pre-staging/tray sequence.
- Production thresholds: no more than 60 incremental staff minutes; at least 44 complete seven-ounce portions.
- Price: $18 per plate. Food cost: $146 per run. Incremental labor valuation: $24/hour.

Run evidence

June 28
- Production: 316 cooked ounces (19 lb 12 oz); 45 complete seven-ounce portions plus 1 cooked ounce; 57 incremental minutes; no sequence deviation.
- Sales/disposition: 45 plates prepared; 43 sold; 2 portions chilled for staff meal under the food-handling procedure.
- Economics: $774 revenue; $22.80 incremental labor; $605.20 contribution after food cost and incremental labor.
- Controls: met both production thresholds.

July 26
- Production: 44 complete portions; 59 incremental minutes; tested sequence used.
- Sales/disposition: 44 plates prepared; 40 sold; 4 portions handled under the approved staff-meal procedure.
- Economics: $720 revenue; $23.60 incremental labor; $550.40 contribution after food cost and incremental labor.
- Controls: met both production thresholds.

August 16
- Production: 45 complete portions; 56 incremental minutes; unchanged tested sequence used.
- Sales/disposition: 45 plates prepared; 44 sold; 1 portion retained for staff meal.
- Economics: $792 revenue; $22.40 incremental labor; $623.60 contribution after food cost and incremental labor.
- Controls: met both production thresholds.

Evidence-based conclusions

Production
- All three controlled runs met the labor ceiling and minimum-yield requirement.
- Results were tightly grouped: 56–59 incremental minutes and 44–45 complete portions.
- With the same 30-pound case and tested pre-staging sequence, the run evidence supports repeatable production under these controls. It does not establish performance outside this controlled plan.

Customer demand
- Sell-through varied across runs: 43 of 45 portions on June 28, 40 of 44 on July 26, and 44 of 45 on August 16.
- The July run showed weaker demand than the other two; the August run recovered to near-full sell-through.
- The evidence supports customer demand as present but variable, rather than uniformly predictable full sell-through. Unsold portions occurred in every run and were recorded through the approved staff-meal disposition.

Economic context
- Each run produced positive contribution after the fixed $146 food cost and measured incremental labor: $605.20, $550.40, and $623.60 respectively.
- These figures are run-level contribution evidence, not a claim of full profit or a forecast.

Archive boundary
This sheet preserves the three-run evidence and its limits. No new menu decision, menu reopening, standing-special claim, or additional operational authorization is made here.
